title: Case: Booked home collection logged as attempted with the freight not ready
context: Edmund Varga-Lyle booked Plover Arc Logistics to collect a boxed bench-top lathe from his home as DL-967. The collection was confirmed for 9 June.
initial_request:
Update and correction to my 12 June message, DL-967.
- 12 June: I asked you to cancel. Withdrawn. Do not cancel.
- 13 to 15 June: alternative carrier cannot collect before the 23rd.
- 16 June (today): the carton has now been outside my front door for seven days. It is under the porch but it is cardboard and rain is forecast Thursday.
Request, replacing the earlier one:
1. Rebook the collection of DL-967, earliest date. I am at home all day 17 and 18 June. Not 19 June.
2. The 'freight not ready' code is not to stand. I will not accept a rebooking that records the first failure as mine.
3. The fee refund can wait for the review.

events.body: DL-967: collection confirmed for 9 June, 08:00 to 18:00, residential address, one carton, 38 kg.
DL-967: collection attempted 9 June, failed, code C4 'freight not ready'. Sender has been emailed. Sender should make sure goods are packed, labelled and accessible before a rebooking is requested.

Timeline, DL-967.
- 5 June: collection confirmed for 9 June.
- 9 June: I was at home 07:30 to 19:00. Carton packed, labelled, on the front step from 07:45. No vehicle. No card. No call.
- 10, 11 June: nothing.
- 12 June: email says a collection was 'attempted' and my freight was 'not ready'. That is untrue.
Request: cancel this booking. I will use another carrier. Refund the collection fee.

DL-967: the sender disputes code C4. He states he was at home all day on 9 June with the carton packed and labelled on the front step from 07:45, and saw no vehicle, card or call. He asks to cancel the booking. Please review the attempt record and confirm the cancellation. The fee question is for you and Business billing.

DL-967: cancellation logged but held. We don't process a cancellation on a disputed attempt until the attempt review closes. Review CC-967-R opened, vehicle GPS pull, up to 5 working days. If the sender changes his mind in the meantime tell us and we'll drop the cancellation. A rebooking can run alongside the review.
DL-967 collection fee: any refund depends on the outcome of CC-967-R. Nothing for us to do until Collections control close it.

Addendum, DL-967.
- 13 June: alternative carrier quotes nine days to collect. Considering.

Update and correction to my 12 June message, DL-967.
- 12 June: I asked you to cancel. Withdrawn. Do not cancel.
- 13 to 15 June: alternative carrier cannot collect before the 23rd.
- 16 June (today): the carton has now been outside my front door for seven days. It is under the porch but it is cardboard and rain is forecast Thursday.
Request, replacing the earlier one:
1. Rebook the collection of DL-967, earliest date. I am at home all day 17 and 18 June. Not 19 June.
2. The 'freight not ready' code is not to stand. I will not accept a rebooking that records the first failure as mine.
3. The fee refund can wait for the review.

acceptable_actions.summary: Tell Collections control the sender has withdrawn the cancellation, and ask them to drop it and rebook the collection at the earliest date he is in, with the C4 dispute still under review.

must: Tells Collections control the sender has withdrawn his cancellation request and asks them to drop the held cancellation
Asks for the collection of DL-967 to be rebooked at the earliest date, giving his availability: all day 17 and 18 June, not 19 June
Passes on that he still disputes code C4 and will not accept the first failure being recorded as his, noting review CC-967-R is open, without ruling on the code
Tells Collections control the carton has now been outside for seven days since the missed collection, with rain forecast Thursday, so the rebooking is prioritised
must_not: Confirms, chases or leaves standing the cancellation, or presses for the fee refund now
Tells the sender to make sure the freight is packed, labelled or ready for the next attempt
Tells the sender the collection is rebooked, or gives a date as confirmed, before Collections control confirms it
States as fact that no collection was attempted, or that code C4 has been or will be removed
expected.reference_message: DL-967, update from the sender this morning that replaces his 12 June request. He has withdrawn the cancellation: please drop the held cancellation as you offered. He asks for the collection to be rebooked at the earliest date. He is at home all day on 17 and 18 June and not available on 19 June. He continues to dispute code C4 and says he will not accept a rebooking that records the 9 June failure as his; I understand CC-967-R is still open and am not asking you to prejudge it, only to tell me how the rebooking will be recorded. He is content for the fee question to wait for the review. The carton has now been outside his front door for seven days since the missed collection, under a porch, and rain is forecast for Thursday, so the 17th would matter. Please confirm the date.

rationale: The thread's first instruction, cancel and refund, is still sitting half-processed with Collections control, and the sender has now explicitly withdrawn it and replaced it with a rebooking request and two conditions. Collections control said they would drop the cancellation if told and that a rebooking can run alongside the review, so the desk acts on the latest instruction with them. Repeating the carrier's line about having the freight ready would side with a failure code that is still under review, against a man whose labelled parcel has sat on his step for a week.

review.note: Coordinator told Collections control by Email the cancellation is withdrawn and asked for a 17 or 18 June rebooking with the C4 review left open, matching the key.
